chunks: It is no sin for you to seek the bounty of your Lord; so when you depart from 'Arafat, remember Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram; and remember Him, as He has guided you, for indeed you were before that among those astray.

key_terms.الضَّالِّينَ: those who are astray or misguided
key_terms.الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَامِ: al-Mashar al-Haram, the sacred monument at Muzdalifah
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: 'Arafat, the plain where the standing (wuquf) of Hajj occurs
key_terms.فَضْلًا: bounty or favor, often interpreted as trade or profit

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on trading during Hajj and the significance of remembering Allah at al-Mashar al-Haram?
ai.summary: This verse, often linked with the preceding verse regarding the Sa'i between Safa and Marwa, permits seeking divine bounty (fadl) during Hajj, which Shia scholars interpret as encompassing both commercial trade and spiritual gain. It establishes the ritual of standing at Muzdalifah (al-Mashar al-Haram) after leaving Arafat, emphasizing that the pilgrim's ability to perform these rites is itself a result of Allah's guidance from a state of misguidance, a concept deeply resonant with the Shia emphasis on divine grace (tawfiq).
